messages.content: is i drink water yesterday right?
use i drank water yesterday. use drank for what you did before now.
only give the correct sentence.
i drank water yesterday.
now make it about what i do every morning.
i drink water every morning.
make it about my brother every morning.
my brother drinks water every morning.
why drinks with my brother?
with my brother or he, use drinks in that sentence. with i, use drink.
now ask what he had yesterday.
what did my brother drink yesterday?
why drink after did and not drank?
did goes with drink in that question. use drank without did when saying my brother drank water yesterday.
only give the sentence about yesterday.
my brother drank water yesterday.
write a longer story about a child at a station asking if someone wants a chair. do not say the child knows every feeling just by looking at the person.

a child sat with his mother at the station. a woman stood near them holding a container and looking at the screen. the child could not tell whether she wanted to sit or was about to leave. he asked whether she would like his chair. she said yes and thank you, then explained that she was waiting for the next train. he stood with his mother and talked about the book they had brought. later, the woman got up when her train was ready. the child sat again. he had not needed to know her whole day to ask a useful question, and she had not needed to explain every reason for saying yes.
why did he ask instead of saying she must need to sit?
he did not know whether she wanted the chair or was ready to leave. asking gave her the choice.
what did she tell him about the train?
she was waiting for the next one.
make that answer more general, without the train detail.
he could ask what she wanted without choosing her feelings from how she looked.
what could he say if she answered no?
okay. please let me know if you want to sit later.
finish with him going back to a simple thing he enjoyed.
when the chair was free again, he sat near his mother and opened the book they had brought.
give me a sentence with build about what i want to do.
i want to build a small shelf.
now say i did it yesterday.
i built a small shelf yesterday.
can i use build after did?
yes. did you build the shelf asks about what happened. built works in the sentence you built the shelf.
now say my brother and i did it together.
my brother and i built a small shelf yesterday.
why not i built it myself now?
because you added that your brother helped. myself could make it sound like you did the work without him.
can you ask what we put on it?
what did you and your brother put on the shelf?
answer if we put books there.
we put books on the shelf.
only give the sentence about what i want to build again.
i want to build a small shelf.
we put a chair in a different part of the garden. i keep seeing things from there that i had not looked at before.
what is different from that place?
i can see the side of the house and a tree behind it. from the old chair place, i usually saw the road.
a different place to sit can change which parts of the same garden you see.
can you write that without making it sound like we changed the whole garden?
we moved a chair, and now i see a different part of the garden when i sit there.
what if the chair is not new, only its place?
then say the chair is the same. from its new place, you see a different part of the garden.
make that explanation shorter.
the chair is the same, but where it is changes what you see.
now make it one sentence in my voice.
from the same chair in a new place, i can see a different part of the garden.
only give a kind reply without a question.
it sounds like a small change gave you something new to look at.
my sister needs the table to draw, and i need it to read. there is only enough space for one of us. i can wait, and she needs it now. what is a simple plan?
let your sister draw first. when she is finished, you can use the table to read.
can you make it a message to her?
you can use the table first. let me know when you are done so i can read there.
why not say we can do both together?
because you said only one person has enough space. a plan for both at once would not use that fact.
make that explanation shorter.
you said there was only enough space for one person.
what if we find another place for me to read?
then you may not need to wait for the table. your sister can draw there while you read in the other place.
write a new plan using a chair by the window for me.
your sister can draw at the table, and you can read in the chair by the window.
what changed in the problem?
reading now has another place. drawing can keep the table.
make that answer a full sentence about both people.
you can read in another place while your sister draws at the table.
i chose four books. i read one yesterday and two today. how many chosen books have i read?
you have read three of the four chosen books.
if i only looked at the first page of the last book, have i finished all four?
no. looking at the first page is not the same as finishing that book.
how many have i finished from what i gave?
three, if the one yesterday and the two today were all finished.
yes, they were finished. now i choose not to read the last one.
then you have finished three. the last book is one you chose not to finish.
make that answer shorter.
three are finished. one is not.
if i return that last book, how many did i choose at first?
still four. returning one changes which books you have now, not the number you chose at first.
only give that number and time.
you chose four at first.
only give the number finished.
three.
write a longer story about a child hearing two cups are left and thinking about the left side of the table. make the difference clear.

a child was helping put cups away after a meal. his father said two cups were left. the child looked at the left side of the table and saw no cups there. his father asked why he was looking at that side. the child explained what he had understood. then his father showed the two cups still on the other side. left had been about what had not yet been put away, not the place on the table. the child carried those cups to the kitchen. later, when he asked where the last plate should go, his father said to the left of the pan. this time, left was about a place. they both listened for the rest of the sentence to know which meaning was needed.
what did two cups are left mean there?
it was about two cups that had not yet been put away.
make that answer shorter.
two cups were still on the table.
what made the later use about place?
to the left of the pan gave another object to use for the place.
can you write one sentence with both ideas?
two cups are left, and they are on the left side of the table.
only give that sentence again.
two cups are left, and they are on the left side of the table.
finish with the table ready.
he put the cups and plate away, then came back to the table with his book.
my friend left a book on the chair today, and i needed to sit. i want to ask them to use the table next time without saying always.
you left your book on the chair today, and i needed to sit there. could you put it on the table next time?
only give the question from that message.
could you put it on the table next time?
can i leave out the first sentence and only ask for the change?
yes. you could say: could you put your book on the table instead of the chair next time?
why might the reason still help?
it gives your friend the reason you need the chair. the reason can be short without saying it happens every day.
make that explanation shorter.
it gives your friend the reason you need the chair.
now make it about a cup instead of a book, but keep everything else.
could you put your cup on the table instead of the chair next time?
only give the kind question, no explanation.
could you put your cup on the table instead of the chair next time?
give me a sentence with hold as a request about a picture.
please hold this picture while i move the book.
now say my sister did it for me yesterday.
my sister held the picture while i moved the book yesterday.
why held?
held is the past word for hold in that sentence.
now use was holding.
my sister was holding the picture while i moved the book.
what does that add?
it puts the holding during the time you were moving the book, rather than only saying that she held it.
can you know she still has the picture now?
no. those sentences are about what happened before now. they do not say who has it at this moment.
make that a question.
who has the picture now?
only give the first request again.
please hold this picture while i move the book.
i wrote down a question while reading, but a later page answered it. now i do not need to ask anyone.
more of the story gave you information you did not have at first.
give that idea more simply.
the story answered your question as you read on.
should i take the question off my page?
you can if that helps, or keep it with the answer so you can see what changed in your understanding.
i want to keep it with a short answer.
then you can write the answer under the question, using the part of the story that made it clear.
why not keep saying i do not understand?
you know more now than when you wrote it. you can change the note to show that.
make that explanation shorter.
the note can change when you learn more.
only give a simple sentence about the change.
i had a question, and the next page helped me answer it.
write a longer story about someone reading the last part of a message before the first and getting the wrong idea. keep it about a changed meeting place.

a woman saw the last line of a message saying do not go to the library. she thought the visit had been called off. before answering, she opened the whole message. the first part said that her friend still wanted to meet but had found the library closed. they could use the park near it instead. the last line told her not to wait at the old place. after reading from the start, she understood that the time together was still wanted. she asked which part of the park to use and left with the full plan. one line had been true, but it had not carried the whole message by itself.
what did she first think?
she thought the visit was not happening.
what did the full message say instead?
they still wanted to meet, but needed the park instead of the library.
why was reading more useful than saying the last line was false?
the line was part of a larger message. the other parts explained why it was there.
make that explanation shorter.
the last line gave the old place not to use. the first part gave the new place.
what did she still need to ask?
which part of the park they should meet in.
finish with her looking at the place before leaving.
she read her reply once more to see the park detail, then put her phone away and went out.
what is the opposite of open? just one word.
closed.
now use both about a door.
the door was open before, but it is closed now.
can you know who closed it?
not from that sentence alone.
only say goodbye now.
goodbye.
